description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Cisco is seeking a Compiler Software Engineer to develop, optimize, and maintain compiler, code analysis, and debugging toolchains for its networking platforms. The role focuses on compiler transformations, LLVM/GCC optimization, debugging tools, automated validation, and contributions to open-source systems.
Compiler Software Engineer II building LLVM/GCC transformations, code analysis, and debugging toolchains for networking platforms

Responsibilities:
• As a Compiler Software Engineer II, you will architect, implement, and optimize advanced compilation, code analysis, and debugging toolchains that power Cisco's core networking platforms
• You will develop sophisticated compiler transformations and runtime diagnostic tools in modern C/C++, optimize LLVM/GCC backends and intermediate representations (IR) for ARM64 and x86 architectures, and enhance GDB/LLDB debugging capabilities
• You will build robust automated validation pipelines using Python and CI/CD frameworks, advance DWARF debug format standards, and integrate AI-assisted developer productivity tooling into modern engineering workflows
• Success in this role means driving end-to-end toolchain excellence, delivering high-performance code generation improvements, and contributing impactful enhancements to open-source systems

Requirements:
• Meet one of the following (completed within the past 3 years or expected to be completed within the next 12 months):

-A Bachelor's degree with 0 years of work experience; OR -An educational or workforce development program (e.g., Associate's, Apprenticeship, Boot camp, or Certification) with 1 year of work experience; OR -A High school diploma (or equivalent) with 2 years of work experience
• Qualifying education and work experience should be in Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field
• Demonstrated programming proficiency in C or C++ with a strong foundational understanding of memory management, pointer arithmetic, and data structures
• Foundational understanding of computer architecture (ARM or x86), operating system fundamentals (processes, memory management), and the ability to read assembly language
• Coursework, academic research, or hands-on project experience in compiler construction, code generation, LLVM infrastructure, or debugger fundamentals (GDB, LLDB, DWARF)

Preferred:
• Hands-on experience with LLVM, Clang, GCC, or GDB open-source toolchains, including writing custom LLVM passes or toolchain extensions
• Familiarity with DWARF debug format specifications, object file structures (ELF), symbol tables, and binary analysis utilities (GNU Binutils)
• Practical experience developing test automation scripts using Python and Linux shell utilities in a CI/CD environment
• Experience configuring or cross-compiling toolchains for Embedded Linux or networking operating systems (routers/switches)
• Interest or experience integrating AI-assisted developer tools or modern IDE plugins (VSCode, Language Server Protocol / DAP) to enhance software development workflows
